Reference / web/routing

web/routing#

Route tables built from controller actions.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

WebRoutes(
    Around(AccessLog(Stdout())),
    Get(path: "/health", endpoint: system.health),
    Scope("/api",
        Resource("/notes", Get(notes.list), Post(notes.add)),
        Resource("/notes/:id", Get(notes.show), Delete(notes.remove)),
        Scope("/users", UserExceptions(),
            Post(path: "", endpoint: users.register),
            Get(path: "/:id", endpoint: users.show),
        ),
    ),
    Fallback(system.missing),
);

Description#

Route tables built from controller actions. An endpoint is any bound action of type async (WebRequest) is Responding, so one controller object can serve many routes and keep its dependencies in its own fields:

Get, Post, Put, Patch and Delete route one method; Route(method:, path:, endpoint:) routes any other, such as OPTIONS, and Any(path:, endpoint:) every method. A Resource writes its path once for several methods. Without a Fallback, a request no route matches is answered 404 with a problem body.

Everything compiles into one std http/routing.Routes, so its rules are kept: a request goes to the most specific pattern (/users/me before /users/:id, /files/:name before /files/*path), two routes of one method with the same shape are refused at construction, a known path with another method gets 405 with Allow, and HEAD uses GET. Requests Routes rejects itself (405, malformed path) are answered by WebRejection as problem replies, Allow included.

Paths: a Scope prefix starts with "/" and does not end with it. A route path is "" (the scope or resource itself, only inside one) or starts with "/". The full pattern is the concatenation of prefixes and the route path.

Around a route run the exception scopes and the Arounds of the table, the Scopes and the Resource it stands in: outer before inner, and within one of them in the order they are written. An ExceptionScope translates the errors it knows into replies; unknown errors propagate to the next outer scope. After all of them, the framework itself answers: a thrown Exception becomes its problem reply. Request bodies are read through web/request.RequestJson, which raises its own 422 Exception; JSON errors from server-side data are not translated. Any other error propagates to the std HttpServer, which answers 500 without a body; cancellation and timeouts keep their std meaning.

Public API#

role ExceptionScope#

role ExceptionScope

Turns the exceptions of endpoints into replies.

ExceptionScope.scoped#

async scoped(request is WebRequest, endpoint is async (WebRequest) is Responding) is Responding

Runs endpoint and replies to what it throws.

role Surrounding#

role Surrounding

Code around endpoints, put into a table with Around (#77): an access log, authentication, headers for every reply. around() gets the request and the rest of the chain as inner. It may answer by itself without calling inner, as a refused login does, or call inner and work with its reply. An Exception thrown further in reaches it as its problem reply; other errors pass through.

Surrounding.around#

async around(request is WebRequest, inner is async (WebRequest) is Responding) is Responding

Runs inner for request, with code before and after: logging, authentication, compression.

object Resource#

object Resource does WebRouting

Several methods on one path, written once (#78):

Resource("/notes", Get(notes.list), Post(notes.add)),
Resource("/notes/:id", Get(notes.show), Put(notes.replace), Delete(notes.remove)),

The routes in it take no path of their own. An Around among them wraps only the resource's routes.

object Around#

object Around does WebRouting

Code around every route of the table, Scope or Resource it stands in (#77):

WebRoutes(
    Around(AccessLog(Stdout())),
    Get(path: "/notes", endpoint: notes.list),
    Scope("/admin", Around(BearerAuth(token: secret)), Get(path: "/stats", endpoint: admin.stats)),
)

A request no route matches passes through the table's Arounds on its way to the Fallback. Requests the table refuses before any route (405, a malformed path) do not. Before a WebSocket upgrade, an Around that calls inner lets the upgrade go on, and one that answers by itself refuses it with that answer.

object Slashes#

object Slashes does WebRouting

What WebRoutes does with a path that differs from a route only by its final slash (#105). By default it answers 308 to the declared form, so /notes/ reaches /notes; WebRoutes(Slashes(SlashPolicy.strict), …) sends such paths to the Fallback instead. Only at the top of WebRoutes.

object Files#

object Files does WebRouting

Files below root at path (#107), with validators, ranges and the Content-Type of each name:

WebRoutes(
    Files(path: "/assets", root: assets, cache: "public, max-age=31536000, immutable", tags: FileTags.content),
    Files(path: "", root: site, cache: "no-cache"),
)

GET and HEAD of path/<name> read root/<name>; a directory answers with its index.html. cache: is the Cache-Control of every file, "" for none; tags: makes ETags from metadata (the default) or from content, the same on every replica (#109). The Arounds of the table pass over files too, and a more specific route below path still wins.

Files.Files#

Files(path is string, root is FileRoot, cache is string = "", tags is FileTags = FileTags.metadata)

Serves root at path; cache becomes Cache-Control, tags picks ETags.

object WebSocket#

object WebSocket does WebRouting

A WebSocket at path (#220): an upgrade is answered with the defaults (the Origin must be the server's own, default limits, 5 seconds to open) and the connection goes to application:

WebRoutes(Get(path: "/", endpoint: site.page), WebSocket(path: "/chat", application: chat))
